title: The Number That Comes Up
logline: At a dry-zone town junction, a lottery-ticket seller's daily calling turns into a private ritual for regulars who buy the same numbers morning after morning, certain today might finally be the day.
human_question: What does it mean to want the same thing every single day, without ever quite expecting to get it?

premise.story: A day in the working life of a lottery-ticket seller at a bus-stand kiosk: the regulars who buy without looking up, the newcomer who is talked into a ticket, the small television playing the evening draw, and the seller's own quiet accounting of who wins and who doesn't.
premise.place: A bus-stand or town-junction kiosk in the dry zone, where tickets, tea and talk move at the same unhurried pace all day.
premise.experience: The viewer falls into the daily rhythm of hope sold in small paper slips: routine, patter, brief excitement, and the evening moment when the numbers are read out.

concept_links.why: The seller's calling is itself the 'prompting' that turns a passing thought into a purchase, while regulars buy the same numbers unprompted and out of habit; the same reaching for a ticket appears with flat routine in most and with real excitement on a lucky day [C006-M:L5] [C006-P:L44].
The ticket seller is one of the concept's own story seeds: reaching for a hoped-for good as part of an ordinary sense-sphere day of sight, sound and small transaction.

what_camera_could_observe: The seller's calls and patter through the morning
A regular buying the same numbers without a word
A newcomer being talked into a first ticket
The small television during the evening draw
Tickets checked, torn or kept for tomorrow
what_must_be_real: The seller's real trade, the regulars' real habits and their own words about why they play. No arranged win or loss.

possible_arc.opening: Dawn at the kiosk; the first calls of the day.
possible_arc.turn: The draw airs on the small television; faces watch, and the numbers don't match.
possible_arc.ending_open: Whatever the seller and regulars actually do the next morning leads the ending.

position_hint: opening candidate: a plausible first film for Group 2, built on daily, ordinary wanting rather than a single big want; a natural place for Object 2's acquisition if a real moment allows (something small changing hands, kept or given).

requirements: An active ticket kiosk with a willing seller
Regular customers willing to speak about their habit
A working evening draw broadcast on site

suggestions.name: A bus-stand or town-junction kiosk in Anuradhapura
suggestions.why: A well-known dry-zone town with an active bus stand and daily lottery trade.
suggestions.verify: No seller has been contacted; exact kiosk and willingness to be filmed are unverified.

risks: Sneering at poor buyers or the seller's trade
Turning gambling into a moral lesson
Privacy of regulars who may not want their habit shown
drop_if: No seller or regulars are willing to be filmed and speak honestly about the habit

connections.note: Hope bought in small doses here meets hope refused all at once there.
